primary_claim: Introducing artificial inference-time latency ('slowdown') into a GPT-3.5-Turbo-16k agent playing TextStarCraft II causes its win rate against a fixed weak (Level 1) built-in AI to collapse from 10/10 at 0% slowdown to 0/10 at 500% slowdown, showing that a pure reaction-speed disadvantage, with decision quality held constant, is enough to make a qualitatively stronger AI agent lose to a much weaker one.

effect.metric: win rate (out of 10 games) vs. Level 1 built-in StarCraft II AI, by slowdown percentage

contradicts_or_qualifies: The original TextStarCraft II paper reported GPT-3.5-Turbo-16k achieving a 50% win rate against the Level 5 (Hard) built-in AI in non-real-time play; replicating this in real-time play (required for the slowdown manipulation) dropped the win rate against Level 5 from 50% to 0%, so the author switched to a Level 1 opponent for the slowdown experiments
stated_future_work: Conduct a proof of concept to more directly test whether weaker intelligences can capably supervise stronger intelligences given a large relative advantage in compute speed
Revisit a Christiano-style capability amplification/iterated amplification scheme, varying compute speed instead of number of agents
Substitute higher-capacity or more intelligent 'reasoning' AIs to test whether greater reasoning ability lets an agent anticipate enemy moves despite slowdown
limitations_stated: Real-time play, required for the slowdown manipulation, degraded performance so much that the built-in AI opponent had to be downgraded from Level 5 to Level 1 for the experiment to be feasible
In RL agents, speed-related decision-making could in principle be trained away via extensive self-play, so results may not generalize beyond inference-time-reasoning setups like this one
Whether the slowdown-driven catch-up effect generalizes across all levels of intelligence or intelligence differential (e.g. very large capability gaps) remains unclear
quote: succumbing to a very easy, very narrow rule-based AI whose *only advantage is speed*.
